MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read comments on role-restricted posts via the Latest Comments block. Attackers can view pages hosting the block, where get_the_ID() checks the host page and get_comment_excerpt() bypasses filtering, exposing restricted comments, post titles, and links.

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.

anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Decoder.readOneValue in bencode/decode.go that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying deeply nested bencode data. Attackers can deliver crafted .torrent files or magnet link metadata with millions of nested lists to cause a fatal stack overflow, or deeply nested v2 file trees to exhaust CPU.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

Opencast before 20.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in WorkspaceImpl.toWorkspaceFile that allows authenticated ingest users to write files outside the workspace root via unvalidated element paths. Attackers can submit media packages whose element URIs or identifiers contain ../ sequences, causing Workspace.get to create directories and write fetched content with Opencast process privileges.

binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption(). Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled.

simple-git before 4.1.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the allowUnsafePack guard by supplying the --exec option to non-push git operations. Attackers who influence arguments passed to listRemote() or raw() can inject --exec for ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack to execute commands on the host.

Delta Sharing reference server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows share recipients to read unshared data via container-scoped Azure SAS tokens. Recipients with a valid bearer token can request credentials from the temporary-table-credentials endpoint to read every blob in the storage container, including unshared tables.

Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 contains a terminal escape sequence injection vulnerability that allows attackers to emit escape sequences by crafting malicious file or archive member names. When a victim highlights such an entry in the choose-files kitten preview panel, unsanitized names are written raw, enabling OSC 52 clipboard overwrites, OSC 8 links, window title changes, or screen spoofing.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 contains a link following vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to read host files by setting --eventpath in an untrusted project .actrc to a symlink. Attackers can commit an event.json symlink pointing to files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa, which act copies into the job container as GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for workflow steps to exfiltrate.

Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment variable values.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translated as SQL. A dollar quote whose tag has a non-ASCII symbol or space is not recognized. An `E''` string with a doubled quote is scanned as a standard string. `{fn right}` and `{fn timestampdiff}` with a negative argument produce a `--` comment. In each case text that the application quoted correctly can run as SQL with the privileges of the application's database role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or configuration reload can turn the setting off during a session. A parameter value with a backslash and a quote then ends the literal, and the rest of the value runs as SQL. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server reads the bytes that follow as the rest of it. The bytes of a value uploaded later on the same connection can then run as a SQL command. Since 42.6.0 a setBinaryStream() value without a length that is executed again throws such an exception, as does the driver's own retry after SQLState 0A000 or 26000. An application stream that throws an unchecked exception has the same effect in all versions. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=prefer, or no TLS before 42.2.5. A service given in the Properties instead of the URL is ignored, so the sslmode of its pg_service.conf entry is lost. BaseDataSource.setUrl() keeps an sslmode, channelBinding or gssEncMode that was set before it. An attacker on the network path can then read and change the traffic. Versions 9.4.1208 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. The driver also shares one MessageProp between reading and writing. One integrity-only packet from the server then makes the driver send later SQL and parameters without encryption. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different number without an error. For example 999999.99e-262144 is stored as 999999.99, so a tiny value can pass a range check and be stored as a large one. The driver also computes 10 to the power of the scale first, so a short value such as 1e-200000000 keeps a thread busy for minutes. Versions 42.3.0 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not refuse a NUL character in a startup parameter. The StartupMessage is a list of NUL-terminated strings, so a NUL in the database name, user, currentSchema, options or ApplicationName adds further parameters. %00 in a URL decodes to a NUL. Someone who controls part of the URL or a property can choose another login role or add replication=database, although the connection still has to pass the authentication of that role. On a server that trusts the client, the attacker can log in as any role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ReadFloat in ColladaLoader.cpp because accessor stride and offset bounds are checked only by ai_assert. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose animation accessor describes more values than its float_array holds to read past the array or dereference null, crashing the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an invalid pointer dereference vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportEmbeddedTextures that derives the texture format hint without checking the strchr result. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use of uninitialized resource vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that builds TRIANGLE_STRIP and TRIANGLE_FAN faces from unfilled faces. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file whose strip or fan primitives trigger out-of-bounds reads or null pointer dereferences, crashing the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ColladaParser::ReadPrimitives that allows attackers to exhaust memory via non-numeric index values. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose

index list contains a non-digit character, causing endless zero-index appends until the importing process crashes.

An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at /program/www/ssl_cert.pem and copied to /config/ssl_cert.pem during initialization. When HTTPS is enabled using the default certificate, a network on-path attacker who obtains the firmware image can use the exposed private key to present an identical certificate and intercept HTTPS traffic. HTTPS is disabled by default .


  *  

Only impacts deployments where an administrator enables HTTPS and retains the default certificate. Because the private key is publicly distributed in the firmware image, an on-path attacker can impersonate the device with an identical certificate fingerprint, bypassing fingerprint checks and stored certificate exceptions (potentially capturing credentials if a user clicks through the expired-certificate warning).

XML::Sig versions before 0.74 for Perl allow code execution via a document's Algorithm attribute that verify resolves to a function name and calls.

The text after the last `#` in the DigestMethod and SignatureMethod Algorithm attributes is looked up with Digest::SHA->can. That returns a code reference for any fully qualified function name, Perl builtins in the CORE namespace included. The digest function is called on the canonical form of the referenced element, so the document picks both the function and its argument.

An attacker who can submit a signed document can run a command as the verifying process.

An externally controlled format string vulnerability in the Snapshot CGI components of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to cause repeatable premature termination of affected privileged CGI requests by supplying crafted input.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link upload component allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped upload share link to upload or overwrite files in the shared folder's immediate parent directory due to missing trailing validation prior to path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper input validation vulnerability in the OpenVPN client configuration import feature of ADM allows authenticated administrative users to execute arbitrary operating system commands via a crafted .ovpn profile.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An OS command injection vulnerability in ADM allows an authenticated administrator to create an iSCSI LUN with a crafted name and schedule a snapshot. The scheduler embeds the name in a root cron job without correctly neutralizing shell metacharacters, allowing arbitrary command execution as root when the job runs.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link folder-listing endpoint allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped share link to list directory contents outside the shared folder, including other Samba shares readable by the link creator, because path validation occurs before path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A race condition during docker cp mount setup in Docker Engine allows a malicious container to leave a read-only bind mount writable while an archive is extracted into the container. When copying files into a container, the daemon bind-mounts the container's volumes into a temporary view and applies the read-only flags afterwards, through a path inside the container's filesystem. A process in the container can change that path in between, so the flags are applied to a different mount and the intended bind mount stays writable for the duration of the copy.

In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-10 to 2.0.0-milestone-16, the destination validation of the Operation Delegation feature, introduced to prevent server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-7412), can be bypassed through DNS rebinding.



Before dispatching a delegated Operation invocation, the server resolves the host of the `invocationDelegation` qualifier URI and rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast and cloud metadata addresses. The outbound HTTP client (Reactor Netty), however, performs its own, independent DNS lookup when opening the connection and does not use the validated addresses. An attacker who can create or update a Submodel Operation and controls the DNS records of the delegation host can answer the validation lookup with a public address and the connection lookup with an internal address. No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled.



Invoking the Operation then causes the BaSyx server to send HTTP POST requests to destinations the protection is meant to block, such as services in internal IT/OT networks, loopback-only interfaces, or cloud metadata endpoints. The server can be used to pivot into network segments that are not directly reachable by the attacker.



Only deployments with the Operation Delegation feature enabled are affected. The feature is enabled by default.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-17.

A NULL pointer dereference and invalid memory release in the server discovery component of the MongoDB C Driver may allow an unauthenticated party that controls a server endpoint, or that can alter unencrypted network traffic, to cause a client application to terminate by sending a crafted discovery response.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.9, the nginx reverse proxy configurations shipped with Ditto (Helm chart, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment files) forward a client-supplied

  `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` header to the Ditto gateway on locations that do not apply nginx authentication, such as `/api/2/connections`. nginx selects the location based on the normalized request URI
  but forwards the raw URI, while the gateway does not treat an encoded slash (`%2f`) as a path separator. A crafted request path is therefore routed by nginx through such an unauthenticated location and
  by the gateway to the regular Things and Policies HTTP API, including routes that send live messages to devices. When pre-authentication is enabled (the default of the Helm chart and the Docker Compose
  setup), an unauthenticated remote attacker can impersonate arbitrary policy subjects and read, modify and delete Things, read Policies, send messages to devices and create entities. Additionally, the
  optional Ingress of the Helm chart (Ditto 3.9.0 to 3.9.9) routes requests directly to the gateway without setting or removing that header, and the WebSocket Ingress of the Helm chart of Ditto 3.3.0 to
  3.8.15 does not set it, allowing the same impersonation without path manipulation when pre-authentication is enabled. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-120753.

MongoDB C Driver contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the credential-selection logic used by its AWS authentication mechanism. A process-wide credential cache can take precedence over the credentials supplied for an individual connection, so a connection configured with one set of credentials may instead be authenticated under an identity cached earlier in the same process. A party able to cause the application process to open an additional connection may thereby obtain unintended privileges.

The MongoDB C Driver does not confirm that the party signing a supplied certificate revocation status response is authorized to answer for the certificate being checked. An unauthenticated party that operates the TLS endpoint a client connects to can therefore have a withdrawn certificate accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of the application's database traffic and in the loss of the revocation decision.

A flaw was found in kubevirt Containerized Data Importer (CDI). The CDI clone controller derives the CommonName of a CDI-CA-signed upload client certificate from the tenant-settable cdi.kubevirt.io/uploadClientName PVC annotation without validation, and the upload server authenticates clients only by certificate CA chain and CommonName string match, with no namespace or PVC binding. A namespace user can obtain a valid client certificate and write arbitrary data into any upload-ready PVC in any namespace whose upload Service is reachable from the cluster network, resulting in cross-namespace integrity impact on disk images used by virtual machines.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.0.0 until 3.1.13, the implementation selected signature verification based on the certificate public key while deriving the digest from the peer-controlled signature scheme without validating that the scheme, key type, and hash requirements were consistent. The affected verification functions are verifyKeySignature for ServerKeyExchange and verifyCertificateVerify for CertificateVerify. An unauthenticated network attacker who can redirect a DTLS handshake and obtain the genuine peer certificate can submit crafted handshake signatures that are accepted without possession of the certificate private key. This can let the attacker impersonate the peer and compromise the confidentiality and integrity of protected traffic; checking a WebRTC SDP certificate fingerprint does not prevent the attack because the genuine certificate is presented. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a server with a SessionStore saved the session ID and master secret after ClientKeyExchange, before receiving a valid Finished message and before enforcing the configured client-authentication checks. A remote client can omit its Certificate message, send ClientKeyExchange, leave the first handshake unfinished, and then resume the cached session using the master secret it learned during key exchange. The server must use a SessionStore and negotiate a certificate-based cipher suite. The attack can bypass client certificates required through RequireAnyClientCert or RequireAndVerifyClientCert, or a rejecting VerifyConnection callback. WebRTC users are not affected. The abbreviated handshake can allow unauthorized access to application data. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a listener performing DTLS 1.2 resumption accepted a session created by an outbound client connection without checking which role created it. A malicious server previously contacted by the application can retain the outbound session secret, select the client-side cached session through its session key, and present it to the application's reachable listener when both connections share a SessionStore. The attacker must first complete an outbound connection. WebRTC users are not affected. The listener can accept application data without running its normal PSK callback or client-certificate authentication checks, allowing a peer trusted only for an outbound connection to gain unauthorized listener access. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.0.0 until 3.1.13, peer certificates were parsed and their RSA public keys were passed to handshake signature and certificate-chain verification without an explicit modulus-size limit. A remote peer can provide a certificate with an unusually large attacker-chosen RSA modulus and an invalid signature; no corresponding private key or valid handshake signature is required to trigger the expensive operation. An RSA verification path must execute. A local ECDSA certificate does not prevent the peer from presenting an RSA certificate, and WebRTC deployments can be affected. Repeated or concurrent malicious handshakes can consume substantial CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.4 until 3.1.13, the handshake cache copied and retained submitted messages without deduplicating entries, limiting the entry count, limiting total payload bytes, or stopping new insertions after handshake completion. A remote peer able to deliver suitable DTLS traffic can grow the cache through incoming handshake messages and repeated caching of outgoing retransmissions for the lifetime of the connection. The fragment reassembly buffer's separate size limit does not prevent this issue because completed messages are retained in the append-only handshake cache. Unbounded cache growth can exhaust application memory and cause a denial of service. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 1.2.2 until 3.1.13, the server state machine did not distinguish successful processing of the client certificate flight from completion of the handshake, so later traffic could revisit the same cached Certificate, ClientKeyExchange, and CertificateVerify messages. A malicious client can withhold Finished and send additional handshake traffic. Depending on the configured authentication policy, repeated work can include certificate parsing, handshake signature verification, and certificate-chain verification. The vulnerable endpoint must act as the DTLS server. Pion WebRTC applications are affected when they operate in that role. Repeated or concurrent attempts can consume excessive CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

A potential security vulnerability has been identified in the HP Hotkey UWP Service, which might allow escalation of privilege. HP is releasing mitigation for the potential vulnerability. Customers using HP Programmable Key are recommended to update HP Hotkey Support.

Insert Pages plugin for WordPress (insert-pages) before 3.11.6 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the insert_pages_handle_shortcode_insert() function that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to read draft, pending, scheduled, and private posts they do not own. Attackers can reference sequential post IDs in the [insert page] shortcode to render the full content, title, excerpt, and metadata of unpublished posts, since the function checks a generic read capability instead of enforcing the read_post meta capability tied to post author and status.

Author Avatars List/Block plugin for WordPress before 2.2.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the card_min_width, card_max_width, card_min_height, and card_max_height attributes of the [authoravatars] shortcode. Attackers can supply a value containing a double quote to break out of the card's style attribute and add event handlers, causing the injected script to execute in the browser of any visitor, including editors or administrators who view the rendered user card.

Lookyloo is a web-based URL capture and analysis platform. Prior to the fix, the authorization mechanism for private captures (seed-based access control) was not consistently enforced at the data access layer. The capture_cache method and numerous internal methods (get_info, get_meta, get_statistics, get_modules_responses, get_data, get_video, get_screenshot, get_har, get_cookies, get_storage_state, get_frames, get_console_messages, get_capture, get_ressource, misp_export, lacus_export, ai_export, comparator functions, and others) could be invoked with only a capture UUID without validating the required seed token. This meant that API endpoints and internal code paths that called these methods directly could return private capture data to unauthenticated users or users lacking the correct seed. The before_request hook in the web interface provided a partial check, but the underlying data layer did not enforce it, creating an inconsistent authorization boundary. An attacker who knew or guessed a private capture UUID could potentially access sensitive data including rendered screenshots, HAR files, downloaded files, cookies, storage state, console messages, and MISP exports through various REST API endpoints and web routes. The fix introduces a LookylooPrivateCapture exception raised at the cache layer when a private capture is accessed without a valid seed, refactors the API to pass CaptureCache objects (already validated) rather than raw UUIDs, and ensures all web and API endpoints propagate the session-known seed or admin status to the data access layer. Background processes use an explicit unsafe=True flag to bypass the check, as they operate server-side with full trust.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in vmd_read_packet() in libavformat/sierravmd.c that leaves 16 packet bytes unwritten for Indeo3 frames. Attackers can supply a crafted VMD file with Indeo3 video to expose leftover heap contents in demuxed packets, such as stream-copied output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in opus_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_opus.c that reads the Opus TOC byte from stale buffer memory when parsing empty RTP payloads. A malicious RTSP server or RTP sender can deliver an empty Opus payload to cause incorrect packet durations and leak bits of stale memory through pkt->duration.

FFmpeg 7.0 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all() in libavformat/dvdvideodec.c when parsing menu audio streams. Attackers can supply a crafted DVD image whose menu IFO declares more than 8 audio streams, reading past the audio_control array and crashing applications.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in dxa_read_packet() in libavformat/dxa.c that ignores short avio_read() results for CMAP palette data. Attackers can supply a crafted DXA stream over a stalling network source so uninitialized stack bytes are copied into returned video packets and decoded frames.

FFmpeg 9.0 before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dash_read_header() in libavformat/dashdec.c when building LCEVC stream groups without checking for a missing codecs string. Attackers can supply a crafted MPD manifest with a representation declaring a dependencyId but no codecs attribute to crash applications using the DASH demuxer.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in peak_init_writer() and wav_write_packet() in libavformat/wavenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying audio with zero channels. Attackers can provide a crafted PCM stream declaring no channels for WAV output with peak envelope enabled, causing out-of-bounds writes past peak_maxpos and peak_maxneg arrays, crashes, and potential code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a double free vulnerability in the fill_marker() function of libavformat/imf_cpl.c that frees a Marker label without clearing the pointer when default scope allocation fails. Attackers can supply a crafted Composition Playlist with a Marker Label lacking a scope attribute, triggering a second free in imf_marker_free() under memory pressure and causing memory corruption or a crash.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in avformat_stream_group_create() in libavformat/options.c that sets the group type before allocating parameters. Attackers can supply crafted HEIF/AVIF files whose tile grid parsing under allocation failure makes ff_free_stream_group() dereference a NULL tile_grid, crashing the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_rtmp_packet_write() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that allows malicious RTMP servers to overflow a 16-byte header buffer. Attackers can send a Set Chunk Size packet on a high channel id with an extended timestamp, which handle_chunk_size() echoes back, corrupting the publishing client's stack.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in rdt_parse_packet() in libavformat/rdt.c that allows remote attackers to crash applications by omitting the ASMRuleBook SDP attribute. Attackers can serve an RTSP session selecting RDT transport without ASMRuleBook, then send an RDT data packet to crash ffmpeg or ffprobe.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in rfc4175_handle_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_rfc4175.c that leaks heap contents into decoded video frames. Attackers can send RTP streams containing only some scan lines of a frame, leaving av_malloc buffer bytes uninitialized and exposing process heap memory in displayed, stored or re-streamed video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in vpk_read_header() in libavformat/vpk.c that computes a last block size not divisible by the channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted VPK file with a large channel count so the last audio packet exposes leftover heap memory contents.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow in send_picture() of libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that leaves the bit reader without a buffer, causing a NULL pointer dereference. Attackers can supply a Dirac/VC-2 stream with a picture data unit of about 256 MiB or more to crash applications packetizing it to RTP.

A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.

Reliance on an untrusted source of the client address in the WebSocket listener of the NetBird relay server (relay/server/listener/ws) in NetBird versions 0.31.1 through 0.74.7 allows an attacker with an enrolled peer to spoof the source address of their relay connection. The listener used the values of the X-Real-Ip and X-Real-Port request headers as the remote address of the connection unconditionally, without checking that the request came from a trusted upstream proxy. A WebSocket client that sends both headers makes the relay record and use an arbitrary address for its connection, including in the relay connection log, so a client can hide its real address or attribute its connection to another host. Only the relay server is affected; the NetBird client, including the Android and iOS apps, does not run the relay listener. The issue is fixed in version 0.75.0, which honours these headers only for requests whose direct connection address is in a configured set of trusted proxies and ignores them by default.

The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software. A privileged user inside a guest virtual machine could use this flaw to make the host QEMU process copy parts of its own memory into the guest's memory, where the attacker could read it. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to view portions of the host QEMU process memory from within a guest, potentially exposing sensitive information that could aid in further attacks. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

The fix for CVE-2026-61801 added file type and size checks when parsing user and group files in github.com/moby/sys/user, but did not apply them consistently across all parsing and lookup functions. ParsePasswdFile, ParsePasswdFileFilter, GetAdditionalGroupsPath, ParseSubIDFile, ParseSubIDFileFilter, ParseIDMapFile, ParseIDMapFileFilter, LookupUser, LookupUid, LookupGroup and LookupGid could still read large or unbounded files. An attacker who controls the contents of a user or group file processed by an affected application, such as /etc/passwd or /etc/group from a container image, can cause excessive memory or CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service. Exploitation depends on how the consuming application uses the affected functions. Fixed in v0.5.1 by enforcing the 10 MiB read limit in all affected functions. Docker Engine 29.10.1 includes the fix.

A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image (for example, via USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image) can trigger this flaw without user interaction, as libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events. This could lead to limited information disclosure or denial of service.

Affected is the function get_argument of the file core/modules/views/plugins/views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc of the component Views Module. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The config-import path enforces no 'use PHP for settings' check while the Views PHP-code argument plugin executes eval() without a permission check, confirming the authorization bypass. The vendor explains: "As per our security advisory policy, no security advisory is required when an exploit requires 'advanced permissions'."

A security flaw has been discovered in vanna-ai vanna 2.0.0/2.0.1/2.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is the function _load_index of the file src/vanna/integrations/faiss/agent_memory.py of the component FAISS AgentMemory Integration. Performing a manipulation results in deserialization. The attack needs to be approached locally. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in DWS Antik Browser 1.17.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file src/server/index.ts of the component Local API Server. Executing a manipulation can lead to origin validation error. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in OpenGEXImporter.cpp because InternReadFile does not reset cached importer state between files. Attackers can supply OpenGEX files to applications reusing one Importer instance, causing freed node, camera, and material pointers to corrupt heap memory and crash.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in BVHLoader.cpp that allows attackers to read freed aiNode objects because the mNodes vector is never cleared between files. Attackers can supply multiple BVH files to an application reusing one Importer instance, causing CreateAnimation to copy freed mName data into channel names, crashing the application or exposing heap contents.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the OBJ exporter that allows attackers to corrupt memory via NaN vertex components breaking comparator ordering. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file with NaN texture coordinates or vertex colors that, when exported to OBJ in libc++ builds, writes file-controlled data past a heap buffer and crashes the application.

RayLabsHQ gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the server send HTTP requests by supplying a url to /api/gitea/test-connection or /api/github/test-connection. Attackers can target internal network services and cloud instance metadata endpoints, reading response content leaked through upstream error messages returned by httpGet.

Endurain before 0.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT /api/v1/strava/link endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify Strava integrations using only a victim's strava_state value. Attackers can submit a leaked state with their own OAuth code to link an attacker-controlled Strava account, or an invalid code to remove the victim's integration.

EpicStaff 1.2.0 before 1.3.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in DocumentViewSet download and copy endpoints that allows authenticated users to access other organizations' documents. Attackers holding Knowledge Sources permissions in one organization can enumerate sequential document IDs to download or copy foreign documents, or insert documents into another organization's collection.

HarnessRouter 0.4.2 before 0.32.2 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the self-hosted sign-in UI that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users via the unvalidated next query parameter. Attackers can send crafted login links with an external, protocol-relative, or backslash-prefixed next value so victims are sent to attacker sites after signing in, enabling phishing.

Mercur @mercurjs/core before 2.3.2 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated vendors to access other sellers by substituting the :id path parameter. Attackers can read payment and tax details, overwrite profiles and addresses, and invite, remove, or re-role team members to take over another vendor's store.

plugNmeet-server before 2.5.3 contains an authorization flaw in PollsController.HandleUserSubmitResponse that allows authenticated room participants to submit poll votes as other users by supplying an arbitrary UserId. Attackers can set UserId to another participant's id to cast votes on their behalf or block their legitimate votes, manipulating poll results.

Spug 4.0.0 before 4.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to execute commands by supplying a crafted git URL to the /api/credential/check/ endpoint. Attackers can inject shell metacharacters into the data field passed to git ls-remote with shell=True, executing commands as the Spug service account, which is root in Docker deployments.

Spug before 4.1.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator users to read per-host SSH private keys through the GET /api/host/ endpoint. Users granted a host can read the cleartext pkey field returned by Host.to_view and log in directly over SSH, bypassing Spug's permissions and audit trail even after revocation.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in gf_rtsp_do_deinterleave that allows malicious RTSP servers to hang clients by sending non-RTSP, non-interleaved data. Attackers can answer a client request with a few bytes not starting with '$', 'RTSP', or 'HTTP', causing the RTSP client thread to spin forever and consume a full CPU core.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SDP_ParseAttribute that allows attackers to cause unbounded memory growth via a NUL byte in an a=fmtp line. Attackers can supply a crafted .sdp file or malicious RTSP DESCRIBE response to hang gf_sdp_info_parse and exhaust memory, causing denial of service.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to crash clients by sending MP4V-ES RTP payloads shorter than 4 bytes. A remote RTP sender or malicious RTSP server can send a short packet after a marker-bit packet, causing an unsigned wraparound in the VOP start-code search loop that reads past the buffer and causes denial of service.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to trigger excessive looping by advertising an undersized AU-headers-length. Attackers can send a crafted 22-byte AAC-hbr RTP packet from an RTP sender or malicious RTSP server to run about 2^28 iterations, pinning a CPU core and stalling clients.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the glTF 1.0 importer that allows attackers to read adjacent heap memory by supplying an unchecked KHR_binary_glTF image bufferView. Attackers can craft a glTF or GLB file whose bufferView byteOffset or byteLength exceeds its buffer, disclosing heap memory through embedded texture data or crashing the process.

Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 contains an invalid mesh reference vulnerability in glTF2Exporter::ExportMeshes that causes out-of-bounds access when meshes without faces are skipped during export. Attackers can supply a PLY point cloud or degenerate glTF 2.0 TRIANGLE_STRIP model exported to gltf2 or glb2 to crash the application or trigger out-of-bounds memory reads and writes.

By adding a From header with lowercase name before the actual From header, an attacker could make Thunderbird display a different sender than the one used to verify an OpenPGP signature. Anyone whose key the victim had accepted could send messages that appeared to be validly signed by any other sender. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

By combining several weaknesses, a crafted email could, when opened, inject commands into the authenticated IMAP connection, and load a web page with JavaScript enabled in place of the message. A bare carriage return in a header let the sender set Thunderbird's internal message flags, marking the message as a feed item and allowing its remote content to load. A reference to an embedded part placed inside an attribute value disclosed the message's internal IMAP URL to the sender. The message ID part of IMAP URLs was not validated, so loading a crafted variant of that URL sent arbitrary IMAP commands, which could modify or delete messages and folders. Finally, a frame reloading the message, together with a legacy feed marker in its content, caused the message pane to load a sender-chosen web page with scripting enabled. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

Thunderbird did not compare the signature creation time with the message date for messages that were both signed and encrypted with OpenPGP/MIME. An attacker who had an old signed message could encrypt it to the victim and resend it with a current date, and have it shown with a valid signature, despite the protection added for CVE-2022-2226. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

When a signed OpenPGP/MIME message had no Date header, or one that could not be parsed, Thunderbird did not compare the signature creation time with the message date. For S/MIME messages with more than one Date header, a later Date header could be used for the comparison. An attacker who had an old signed message could resend it and have it shown with a valid signature, despite the protection added for CVE-2022-2226. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

When a CardDAV address book was accessed through an HTTP proxy that requested authentication, Thunderbird could answer the proxy with the CardDAV server's username and password. This affected both setting up a new address book and syncing existing ones, where a saved password could be sent without any user interaction. A malicious or compromised proxy could use this to obtain the address book credentials, even for address books served over HTTPS. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

A received message could include an attachment that referred to an arbitrary local file under a misleading name. If the user dragged that attachment into a message being composed and sent it, the contents of the referenced local file were included in the outgoing message. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

Allot's Subscriber Management Platform (SMP) v18.3.53 stores sensitive configuration credentials protected by a product‑wide, hard‑coded master password. The master key is constructed using a hard-coded string value plus a default key value. This results in an effective encryption key that is recoverable from shipped scripts and configuration files. The platform uses a deprecated and cryptographically insecure algorithm (PBEWithMD5AndDES) and no documented mechanism exists to change the key. An attacker with read access to configuration files, backups, or diagnostic bundles can recover credentials and TLS keystore/truststore passwords, and access to subscriber-management operations and subscriber PII.

A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted JIF image file, a 32-bit integer overflow occurs during the pixel buffer size calculation, while the zlib output limit is computed separately without wrapping. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the compressed image data is decompressed. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

ntop n2n supernode 3.0 through 3.1.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to leak memory and execute code by sending an untrusted 16-bit auth token_size in REGISTER_SUPER_NAK datagrams. Attackers can register an edge in a chosen community, then send an oversized token_size to leak stack canaries and pointers, overwrite the return address, or crash the supernode.

Canvas 7.0.0 before 7.2.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Contributors to inject scripts by exploiting a libxml2 parser differential in PostBody::clean(). Attackers can publish posts with slash-separated event handler attributes rendered unescaped in show.blade.php, hijacking Editor or Admin sessions to escalate their role to Admin.

Marley through 16.8.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated patient-portal users to create payment records against other patients' documents by supplying arbitrary patient and docname values. Attackers can call the get_payment_link endpoint, which saves Healthcare Payment Records with ignore_permissions, to corrupt another patient's payment history and reconciliation data.

Obtainium before 1.7.5 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to write or delete JSON files outside app_data by supplying an app id containing ../ sequences. Attackers can serve an obtainium://app deep link with a crafted id that, once imported, overwrites other app configurations or writes files to shared storage, and later deletes them on app removal.

Obtainium before 1.7.5 trusts the allowIdChange field in imported app data, allowing attackers to bypass the package ID mismatch check by delivering crafted obtainium://app deep links. Once a victim confirms the import, attackers can silently replace a tracked app with an attacker-controlled source and install a different APK, prompt-free when Shizuku or root is authorized.

Thymeleaf before 3.1.6.RELEASE contains a restricted expression mode bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to perform forbidden actions through improperly scoped expression objects. Attackers can inject input into restricted contexts like preprocessing, th:utext, th:on* handlers, fragment names, or TEXT templates to escalate server-side template injection.

BusyBox through 1.38.0 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability in tftpd that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access files outside any intended directory when started without a DIR argument. Attackers can send RRQ or WRQ packets with file names beginning with '/' to read sensitive files like /etc/shadow or overwrite files, typically as root.

OpenResty stream-lua-nginx-module before 0.0.20rc4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows remote peers to trigger access to freed memory when a receiveuntil() pattern iterator is garbage-collected while still referenced by the socket. Attackers can interrupt or close the cosocket connection so later reads or socket closure use the stale pattern pointer, crashing or corrupting the nginx worker.

AppStream 0.14.5 before 1.2.3 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in asc_l10n_parse_data_qt() that allows attackers to hang compose runs by supplying unchecked tag lengths in Qt .qm files. Attackers can place a crafted .qm file with a 0xFFFFFFFB tag length, referenced by a component's qt translation element, to wrap the read offset and hang appstreamcli compose indefinitely.

AppStream 0.14.5 before 1.2.3 contains a division by zero vulnerability in asc_read_translation_status() in compose/asc-utils-l10n.c that allows attackers to crash compose runs via crafted Qt .qm files. Attackers can supply a valid .qm file with no TRANSLATION records, triggering SIGFPE that terminates the entire appstreamcli compose or libappstream-compose process.

rocket.chat Server-Side Request Forgery Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of rocket.chat. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the web service, which listens on TCP port 3000 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a URI prior to accessing resources. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-29853.

Bytebase DBHub MCP Incorrect Authorization Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of Bytebase DBHub. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the implementation of the MCP server. The issue results from an incorrect authorization decision when parsing untrusted SQL. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-27635.

A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The impacted element is the function store of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

A vulnerability has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. This affects the function update of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. The manipulation leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Uploads::saveFile/Auth::init of the file src/Uploads.php of the component Authorization Subsystem. Such manipulation of the argument PicoContentEditorUpload leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

browser-use before 1.0.0 contains a URL parser differential vulnerability in SecurityWatchdog that allows attackers to bypass allowed_domains, prohibited_domains, and block_ip_addresses checks by crafting a URL with a backslash before the allowed host, exploiting the mismatch between urllib.parse hostname extraction and Chromium's WHATWG-style URL parsing. Attackers can influence an LLM-controlled navigate action, such as through prompt injection, to send requests to loopback or private addresses or arbitrary external hosts before the browser redirects to about:blank, enabling SSRF and persistent state changes on the target server.

browser-use before 1.0.0 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability in the SecurityWatchdog's _is_url_match function that allows attackers to bypass domain restrictions by exploiting a raw-string startswith() comparison instead of parsed hostname validation. Attackers can craft URLs using userinfo injection or domain prefix confusion (e.g..com@attacker.com or .com.attacker.com) to redirect an LLM-controlled navigation to an arbitrary host, exfiltrating sensitive data such as secrets embedded in the URL to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

borg-ui before 2.4.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows a repository-scoped operator to escalate to full administrator by exploiting an unrestricted source_directories field in the backup-plan API that lacks path allow-listing. Attackers can configure a backup plan to archive the application's data directory, download the resulting archive to extract the static HS256 .secret_key, and use it to forge a JWT with sub":"admin" to access admin-only endpoints like GET /api/auth/users, achieving full application takeover without admin credentials, XSS, or CSRF.

CubeWP Forms before 1.1.13 contains an unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript by submitting unregistered field names through the public REST route cubewp-custom-form/v1/submit/, which bypasses its own nonce check and saves unsanitized values due to a missing default case in the sanitizer, later rendered unescaped on the admin Leads detail page. Attackers can send a single crafted GET request containing a script payload in a custom form field to execute arbitrary JavaScript in an administrator's wp-admin session when the lead is viewed, enabling full site takeover such as creating a new administrator account.

Devin Desktop Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Devin Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the Electron framework. The product loads a script file from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-33385.

LiteLLM MCP Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of LiteLLM. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of MCP stdio configurations. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-31815.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of the api_base parameter in chat completion requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a URI prior to accessing resources.
